name: zc_avatar_ladder

tests.name: there are Project Avatar figures to spawn
the instrument repeats: one setting read five times disagrees LESS than the settings do

rung_zero_spread.note: the median of these is what the ladder uses; the spread is what says whether it means anything

detail.note: five reads of an unchanged world. If they scatter as widely as the rungs, nothing below is a measurement of avatars -- it is a measurement of this machine. Every cause proposed for the unexplained 106.58 ms at one avatar was, until this ran, a single draw from an unchecked distribution.

tests.name: every rung of the ladder was measured with the clock running
ten Project Avatars still hold a playable frame
the ladder measured avatars and not the machine warming up

detail.note: the same crowd size measured twice in one session, once on the way up and once on the way down. A gap here means the first rung paid for shader compiles the later rungs did not, and every marginal cost derived from the ascending pass is worth nothing.

tests.name: the cost per avatar does not grow as the crowd does

detail.note: the founder: 'Project Avatars must scale inside one Server Avatar.' A system that scales charges about the same for the tenth as for the second; one that does not charges more.

tests.name: arriving avatars do not stall the frame

detail.note: the 95th percentile, not the max: one unrelated shader compile inside a spawn window would otherwise be charged to the avatar, and this project has already read a spawn as SAVING 468 ms for exactly that reason.

rung_zero_spread.note: the median of these is what the ladder uses; the spread is what says whether it means anything
